 Sikkim's birding hotspot map unveiled at international fair in Texas
 GANGTOK,: 
Sikkim's rich avian diversity and potential for nature-based tourism gained 
international visibility with the unveiling of the State’s birding hotspot map 
at the ongoing four-day International Birding Fair in Texas, USA. 
 The 
map was released by Tracy Zervos, one of the organisers of Birdfair Texas, in 
the presence of international participants from the United States and several 
countries, informs a press release. 
 Copies 
of the map were distributed among participants to introduce Sikkim’s diverse 
birdlife, wildlife and prominent birding destinations to the global 
birdwatching community. 
 Dr 
Peter Lobo, Chapter Chairman of the Indian Association of Tour Operators (IATO) 
for Sikkim and North Bengal, is representing the region at the event. He has 
been actively promoting the Sikkim-North Bengal birding circuit and exploring 
opportunities to attract international birdwatchers and nature enthusiasts to 
the Eastern Himalayas. 
 The 
map was conceptualised and designed by Chewang R. Bonpo, president of Sikkim 
Ornithological Society. 
 It showcases 
iconic Himalayan bird species, wildlife and key birding hotspots across Sikkim, 
offering international visitors an overview of the State’s natural heritage and 
its potential as a global birding destination. 
 “The 
initiative goes beyond tourism promotion. Its broader vision is to encourage 
high-value, low-impact nature tourism, creating sustainable livelihood 
opportunities for trained and licensed local bird guides while supporting rural 
homestays and local communities across Sikkim,” the release states. 
 The concept 
of promoting birdwatching tourism internationally was also discussed at the 
recently-held International Tourism Mart (ITM) in Tawang, where State Tourism minister 
Tshering Thendup Bhutia and Tourism secretary Hondala Gyaltsen held discussions 
with Lobo on the proposed Birdfair initiative. 
 These 
discussions helped lay the foundation for promoting Sikkim's birding potential 
on an international platform, the release mentions 
 Lobo 
said the response from international participants at the Texas event had been 
encouraging, with considerable interest in the biodiversity and natural 
landscapes of Sikkim and North Bengal.
